World.title: Anthropic to brief global financial watchdog on cyber flaws exposed by Mythos – report
World.content:
This is AI generated summarization, which may have errors. For context, always refer to the full article.

ANTHROPIC. The Anthropic logo is seen in this illustration taken May 20, 2024.

Anthropic will discuss the capabilities of its new Mythos Preview AI model with leading finance ministries and central banks from the FSB, following a request by Bank of England Governor Andrew Bailey, a Financial Times report says

Artificial intelligence startup Anthropic is set to brief the Financial Stability Board (FSB) on cyber vulnerabilities in the global financial system identified by its latest AI model, Mythos, the Financial Times reported on Monday, May 18, citing people familiar with the plan.

The Claude chatbot-maker will discuss the capabilities of its new Mythos Preview AI model with leading finance ministries and central banks from the FSB, following a request by Bank of England Governor Andrew Bailey, the FT said.

Bailey chairs the FSB, a global risk watchdog responsible for coordinating financial rules for G20 economies.

Anthropic did not immediately respond to Reuters’ request for comment.

An FSB spokesperson said the international body “welcomes engagement with Anthropic and other firms on emerging and frontier risks to global financial stability.”

Mythos, announced last month but not yet released, is a cybersecurity model designed to detect decades-old vulnerabilities in web browsers, infrastructure and software, according to Anthropic.

Cybersecurity experts have warned the system could supercharge more sophisticated cyberattacks, posing a risk to the banking industry reliant on legacy technology systems.

In April, BoE Governor Bailey warned that Mythos could pose major security risks to the cyber world.

“It would be reasonable to think that the events in the Gulf are the most recent challenge to us in this world, until, I think it was last Friday, you wake up to find that Anthropic may have found a way to crack the whole cyber risk world open,” Bailey said at an event at Columbia University in New York last month.

“The issue is: to what extent is this new version of the product going to be able to, in a sense, identify vulnerabilities in other systems which can be exploited for cyberattack purposes,” Bailey said. – Rappler.com

World.title: DOJ recommends plunder, graft cases vs Estrada, Bonoan over flood control mess
World.content:
This is AI generated summarization, which may have errors. For context, always refer to the full article.

The Office of the Ombudsman will still review the recommendation of the Department of Justice, and decide whether or not to file the cases in court

MANILA, Philippines – The Department of Justice (DOJ) recommended the filing of plunder and graft cases against Senator Jinggoy Estrada and former Department of Public Works and Highways (DPWH) secretary Manuel Bonoan over alleged flood control corruption.

The Office of the Ombudsman, on Monday, May 18, confirmed that it has received the DOJ’s resolution recommending the filing of cases against the two.

The recommended cases also include direct bribery and receiving gifts by public officers under Article 210 of the Revised Penal Code, and corruption of public officials under Article 212.

Estrada and Bonoan are already barred from leaving the country after the DOJ secured a precautionary hold departure order against them in February.

Play Video

Apart from Estrada and Bonoan, the DOJ also recommended cases against certain officials of the DPWH.

But the justice department dropped the complaints against former DPWH undersecretary Roberto Bernardo, former district engineer Henry Alcantara, and former regional director Gerard Opulencia, since they are already state witnesses.

The late DPWH undersecretary Cathy Cabral was also removed as a respondent due to her death.

According to the Ombudsman, the DOJ probe centered on allegations that “multiple high-ranking public officials and private individuals conspired to maneuver allocations, rig public bidding processes, and siphon government funds stemming from major national infrastructure budget systems.”

“The preliminary investigation accumulated exhaustive evidence, including legislative records, Position Description Forms, and sworn transcripts from the Senate blue ribbon committee hearings held on November 14, 2025, which detailed illicit maneuvers and alleged 30% cuts surrounding regional flood control projects,” the investigative body said.

It’s important to note that the DOJ only made its recommendation to the Ombudsman, which means the matter has yet to reach a court. It would be the Ombudsman who would file the charges in court, if it agrees with the position of the justice department.

“Moving forward, the next step will be to allow the Office of the Ombudsman to conduct its own independent review and resolution on the merits of the case. The possible outcomes of the office’s independent evaluation include affirming the findings of the Department of Justice, amending the resolution, or reversing the findings altogether,” the Ombudsman said.

As of writing, only a few flood control cases have reached the courts.

Those cases include that of former senator Bong Revilla, former Ako Bicol representative Zaldy Co, and some former DPWH officials which are pending with the Sandiganbayan, and contractor Sarah Discaya’s case before the Lapu-Lapu City Regional Trial Court in Cebu. – Rappler.com

World.title: Padilla, person of interest in Dela Rosa’s escape, shows up in Senate session
World.content:
This is AI generated summarization, which may have errors. For context, always refer to the full article.

SENATE SESSION. Senator Robin Padilla speaks during the plenary session on May 12, 2026.

Asked why Senator Bato Dela Rosa is hiding, Senator Robin Padilla says the former police chief 'doesn't want to be kidnapped'

MANILA, Philippines – Senator Robin Padilla returned to the Senate on Monday, May 18, with his usual swagger and a conspicuous cup of coffee in hand.

But he did not arrive with two things: Senator Ronald “Bato” dela Rosa, who has an International Criminal Court (ICC) arrest warrant linked to his role in the Duterte administration’s bloody drug war, and a clear explanation on the circumstances surrounding his close ally’s departure from the Senate after last week’s shooting incident.

Asked to confirm whether he was with Dela Rosa on the night after the incident, Padilla sidestepped the question, pointing instead to the ongoing investigation.

“Let’s just wait for the official report,” he told reporters on the sidelines of the plenary, while the session was suspended as senators wore their red robes for the convening of the impeachment court.

“Umuwi lang ako ng bahay kasi tatlong araw na akong hinahanap ng asawa at anak ko (I went home because my wife and children had been looking for me for three days),” he said.

Padilla said he and Dela Rosa had been together inside the Senate for three days or from Monday, May 11 to Wednesday, May 13.

Newly installed Senate President Alan Peter Cayetano earlier confirmed that Dela Rosa left the Senate building with Padilla.

The National Bureau of Investigation has tagged Padilla as a “person of interest” in its probe into Dela Rosa’s reported escape.

Pressed on whether he personally drove Dela Rosa out of the Senate, Padilla responded with a grin.

“Nako, intayin niyo ‘yung imbestigasyon (Let’s just wait for the investigation),” he said, pointing and smiling at the reporter who asked the question.

However, Padilla categorically denied he accompanied Dela Rosa to the airport after the senator left the Senate before dawn on Thursday.

Padilla maintained that Dela Rosa has no warrant of arrest.

So, why is the former Philippine National Police chief in hiding?

Dela Rosa is hiding from “kidnappers,” Padilla said, a reference to the claim of supporters of former president Rodrigo Duterte that he was “kidnapped” and brought to the ICC in The Hague, Netherlands in March 2025 to face charges of crimes against humanity for murder.

The Department of Justice and the Office of the Solicitor General, however, have argued the Philippine government may surrender suspects to the ICC under Republic Act No. 9851 or the Philippine Act on Crimes Against International Humanitarian Law, Genocide, and Other Crimes Against Humanity.

Confronted with that legal argument, the actor-turned-politician brushed it aside.

“Let the lawyers argue. As for me, Bato doesn’t want to be kidnapped,” he said.

After six months of being away from public view, Dela Rosa resurfaced in the upper chamber on May 11 to support the Senate coup that installed Cayetano as Senate president. He had also earlier sought refuge in the Senate under what Cayetano described as “protective custody.”

Still, Padilla insisted that Dela Rosa remains in the Philippines. – Rappler.com

World.title: Senate convenes as court. What next for Sara Duterte’s impeachment?
World.content:
This is AI generated summarization, which may have errors. For context, always refer to the full article.

Duterte will have 10 days to respond to the allegations against her, while the House gets five days to comment on the Vice President's response

MANILA, Philippines – The Senate convened into an impeachment court on Monday, May 18, amid the Senate leadership shake-up rumors that swirled over the weekend until Monday.

The convening came after the Senate’s first session after the May 13 shooting incident and Senator Bato dela Rosa’s escape on May 14.

Play Video

Wearing their red robes, the senators took their oath as senator-judges, while Senate President Alan Peter Cayetano assumed the role as the court’s presider.

Play Video

Under the 1987 Constitution, senators serve as judges of the impeachment court tasked to decide whether or not to convict Vice President Sara Duterte. Meanwhile, the prosecutors who will defend the Articles of Impeachment against the Vice President come from the House of Representatives which recently impeached Duterte for a second time with 257 votes.

The Articles of Impeachment which contain the allegations against the Vice President are now with the impeachment court.

Play Video

Cayetano issued a writ of summons, directing Duterte to file an answer to allegations within 10 calendar days upon receipt of the document. The summons, along with a copy of the articles, will be sent by the Senate sergeant-at-arms to the Vice President.

“She is directed to appear before the Senate hall of the Senate of the Philippines upon notice,” the Senate President said.

After receiving Duterte’s reply, the House prosecution team will file their reply within five calendar days.

The pre-trial — the phase where the parties discuss their evidence to be presented during the trial — will happen shortly after. After the pre-trial, Cayetano said the impeachment court will set the schedule for the trial proper.

What if Duterte fails to respond or fails to appear on the day she was summoned? Based on the Senate’s impeachment rules, the “trial shall proceed nevertheless as upon a plea of not guilty.”

Duterte became the first Philippine official to be impeached twice after 257 members of the House of Representatives voted to impeach her again on May 11. This came after the botched proceedings in 2025 caused by the Supreme Court decision that ruled the 2025 Articles of Impeachment as unconstitutional.

The latest allegations against Duterte include her threats to President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. and his family, alleged misuse of confidential funds, and alleged unexplained wealth. – Rappler.com

World.title: Price hike for gasoline, diesel starting May 19 as fuel supply drops to 45 days
World.content:
This is AI generated summarization, which may have errors. For context, always refer to the full article.

PUMP. Motorists refuel their tanks at a gas station in Manila as concerns over rising fuel prices due to the escalating conflict in the Middle East worsen, on March 5, 2026.

Energy Secretary Sharon Garin says the country’s fuel inventory was at 45 days, down from 50 days, but she believes this is 'not alarming'

MANILA, Philippines – Pump prices for diesel and gasoline are set to increase this week while kerosene prices are expected to roll back, the Department of Energy (DOE) announced on Monday, May 18.

Beginning Tuesday, May 19, diesel prices will be raised by around P2.82 per liter while gasoline prices will increase by P1.21 per liter.

Meanwhile, kerosene pump rates will drop by at least P2.21 per liter.

Image from Department of Energy

Energy Secretary Sharon Garin reiterated that the DOE sets the maximum amount that oil companies can raise their pump prices, while the rollback rates are the minimum prices.

“Although we determine the amount, we determine the value based on the reported practice of the companies, which is the replacement cost and using the current freight insurance and premium cost also and transportation, averaging all that,” she explained.

Last week’s price adjustments resulted in gasoline prices in Metro Manila at around P71.80 to P99.08 per liter, diesel at P69.40 to P89.91 per liter, and kerosene at P112.88 to P150 per liter.

Inventory down by 5 days

The DOE also reported that the country’s fuel inventory can now last 45.33 days, lower by around 5 days from the previous week’s average 50.70-day supply.

Image from Department of Energy

Despite the decline in fuel inventory, Garin said this is not a cause for concern since the international supply chain is now becoming more predictable.

“The average as of this week is lower than the previous week but this is not an alarming state because we are assured of supply from other countries,” she said.

According to the DOE’s oil monitor as of May 12, crude oil prices fell after the United States proposed a fresh peace proposal to ease tensions in the Middle. But the DOE noted that the decline was short-lived due to pessimissm over the deal’s outcome.

Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) leaders met in Cebu on May 7 to 8 where the bloc’s leaders discussed fuel supply concerns arising from the ongoing situation in the Middle East.

President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. said the closure of the Strait of Hormuz underscored the need for a reservoir that ASEAN countries can tap during times of crisis.

– Rappler.com

World.title: [Ask the Tax Whiz] BIR clarifies rules on donor’s tax on cash donations
World.content:
This is AI generated summarization, which may have errors. For context, always refer to the full article.

How is the donor’s tax on cash donations filed and paid? Can cash donations be claimed as a deductible expense?

The Bureau of Internal Revenue (BIR) issued Revenue Memorandum Circular (RMC) No. 10-2026 to clarify the tax treatment of purely cash donations, including filing and payment procedures, documentary requirements, deductibility rules, and the applicability of the electronic Certificate Authorizing Registration (eCAR).

Below are the key clarifications taxpayers need to know:

1. Filing and payment procedures for donor’s tax on cash donations, including required documents

How is the donor’s tax on cash donations filed and paid?

Donor’s tax for purely cash donations must be filed electronically through available BIR platforms such as eBIRForms, eFPS, or authorized tax software providers. Payment can be made through Authorized Agent Banks (AABs) or the Bureau’s electronic payment channels.

What documents must be submitted?

The following must be submitted within 30 days from the date of donation to the appropriate Revenue District Office (RDO) or Large Taxpayers (LT) Division:

2. Requirement of Electronic Certificate Authorizing Registration (eCAR) for cash donations

Can cash donations be claimed as a deductible expense? What supports this claim?

Yes, cash donations to accredited donee institutions may be claimed as a deduction from gross income, provided they are properly documented.

The following serve as supporting documents for deduction claims:

Complete set of donation documents listed above

Proof that the donee is accredited (e.g., Philippine Council for NGO Certification or BIR accreditation, if applicable)

Documentation required under Section 34(H) of the Tax Code for deductible charitable contributions

These documents serve as proof of the donation and support future claims for income tax deductions.

3. Is an Electronic Certificate Authorizing Registration (Ecar) required for cash donations?

Do cash donations require an eCAR?

No. The circular explicitly states that an eCAR is not required for purely cash donations.

This is because cash is not a registrable property and does not require transfer of title under any government registry.

RMC No. 10-2026 simplifies compliance by clarifying that while cash donations must still be properly documented and reported, they do not require eCAR, and must follow strict submission and filing timelines to be valid and deductible. – Rappler.com

World.title: Ombudsman serves suspension order on Senate official
World.content:
Acting Senate Sergeant-at-Arms Mao Aplasca —SCREENSHOT FROM YT

MANILA, Philippines — The Office of the Ombudsman on Monday served on acting Senate Sergeant at Arms (SAA) Mao Aplasca a six-month preventive suspension order after he admitted to firing the first warning shot that led to an exchange of gunfire with National Bureau of Investigation personnel in the Senate last week.

“Ombudsman personnel were in Senate to attempt to serve the Order of Preventive Suspension of Acting SAA Aplasca as well as the Subpoena for the CCTV footage [of the shooting incident],” Assistant Ombudsman Mico Clavano said.

He added that they later received confirmation that both documents were received by the Senate secretariat.

Article continues after this 

Ombudsman Jesus Crispin Remulla ordered Aplasca’s suspension on May 15 after he created a team to look into the shooting incident between SAA personnel and NBI agents on May 13, two days after Sen. Ronald “Bato” Dela Rosa showed up at the Senate after being in hiding for over six months.

READ: Senate shooting: Aplasca admits firing first shot at NBI agents

Dela Rosa’s appearance created tension between some senators and the NBI, which had sent two agents to arrest him based on a warrant from the International Criminal Court, which earlier tagged him as a “co-perpetrator” in former President Rodrigo Duterte’s drug war.

Suspect positive for gunpowder

Remulla said the suspension of Aplasca was aimed at preventing anyone from influencing the investigation. He also issued a subpoena for copies of the Senate’s CCTV footage of the incident, saying he would likewise ask for recordings and affidavits from reporters who were there at the time.

Hours after the shooting, Dela Rosa secretly left the Senate, which had placed him under its protective custody to prevent his arrest.

Article continues after this 

A supposed NBI driver who was arrested during the Senate shooting incident has tested positive for gunpowder residue based on the results of his paraffin test, according to the Southern Police District (SPD).

A paraffin test determines the presence of gunpowder residue on a person’s hands, which may indicate if they recently fired a gun.

Article continues after this 

SPD spokesperson Lt. Margaret Panaga, however, told Camp Crame reporters that their investigation is still ongoing, saying: “For now, we can’t give any conclusive details.”

When arrested, Mel Oragon, 40, yielded a brown sling bag containing 30 pieces of cal. 5.56 ammunition; a long magazine with 26 pieces of cal. 5.56 ammunition; and a short magazine with 15 pieces of cal. 9mm ammunition, according to Panaga.

He was also caught allegedly with a blue jacket with NBI markings, a black polo shirt with an NBI logo and a badge, Panaga added.

Oragon has undergone inquest proceedings for alarm and scandal, tumults and disturbances of public order, resistance and disobedience to a person in authority, disturbance of proceedings, trespassing on property, direct assault and violation of Republic Act No. 10591, or the firearms and ammunition regulation law.

Just a volunteer

NBI Director Melvin Matibag had said that Oragon was not an NBI employee but rather a “volunteer.” The Inquirer contacted Matibag for comment on Monday, but as of this writing, he had yet to respond.

President Marcos, meanwhile, contradicted the claim of Senate President Alan Peter Cayetano that the chamber was under attack last week, based on the statements of the NBI and Philippine National Police.

World.title: Gov’t loses P23B in revenues over illegal vapes
World.content:
INQUIRER FILE PHOTO

MANILA, Philippines — Some 86 percent of vapes sold in the Philippines in 2025 were illicit, marking the highest rate among Southeast Asian countries where vaping products remain legal, according to a regional study.

In a report released on Monday, the EU-Asean Business Council and market intelligence firm Euromonitor International estimated that illicit vape sales in the Philippines caused government revenue losses of around $400 million, or roughly P23 billion, from 2024 to 2025 alone.

The report comes amid renewed calls in the Philippines, led by the Department of Health and several lawmakers, to ban vape products altogether or prohibit nontobacco flavors, which regulators say are more appealing to minors.

Article continues after this 

READ: BOC intercepts P1B worth of illegal vape products in Navotas City

Imported from China

“In markets where e-vapor products are legal such as the Philippines, illicit e-vapor products are found to be sold in independent tobacconists, specialty vape shops, etc,” it said.

READ: Push grows to raise vape, tobacco age limit to 25

Illicit vapes are mostly imported from China and are often disguised as ordinary e-commerce parcels because of their compact size and individual packaging, the report said.

While losses from illicit vaping products were substantial, cigarettes still accounted for the bulk of the illegal tobacco trade in the country, costing the government an estimated P141 billion, or $2.5 billion, in foregone revenues over the same two-year period.

This made the Philippines one of the hardest-hit markets in the Asean-6. Indonesia recorded the region’s largest revenue losses at $5.6 billion, while Malaysia also lost about $2.5 billion. /cb

World.title: Ex-student leader among 5 ‘NPA rebels’ killed in Negros
World.content:
RETRIEVAL Residents carry one of the fatalities following a clash between government troops and suspected NPA members in Cauayan, Negros Occidental, on May 16. Authorities said the NPA rebels had been linked to past incidents of violence on Negros Island. —CHENG SANTILLAN/CONTRIBUTOR

BACOLOD CITY, NEGROS OCCIDENTAL, Philippines — A former student leader in Cebu City, who was tagged by the military as a New People’s Army (NPA) member, was among five people killed in an encounter with government troops in Cauayan, Negros Occidental, on Saturday, government officials said on Monday.

The Philippine Army identified the fatality as Vince Francis Dingding, also known as “Poy,” a resident of Capitol Site, Poblacion, Cebu City.

The National Task Force to End Local Communist Armed Conflict (NTF-Elcac) said Dingding had been an active student leader affiliated with Kabataan Party-list Cebu before he was reportedly recruited into the underground youth movement Kabataang Makabayan.

Article continues after this 

READ: 6 civilians among 19 killed in Negros clash, says fact-finding team

In a statement issued on Monday, the NTF-Elcac expressed “deep sadness” over Dingding’s death, describing him as “a former student leader whose life and promise ended in a recent armed encounter in Cauayan, Negros Occidental.”

The task force said his death was “another painful reminder of the continuing tragedy caused by the CPP (Communist Party of the Philippines)-NPA-NDF (National Democratic Front) terror-grooming pipeline,” which it claimed draws young activists from advocacy work into armed struggle.

READ: Alleged rebel killed, 2 firearms seized in fresh Negros clashes

According to the Army, Dingding served as a political instructor of the NPA’s Southwest Front in Negros.

Article continues after this 

The NTF-Elcac said publicly available records showed that he had once been active in student leadership circles within the University of the Philippines (UP) Cebu community.

‘Idealistic’

“He was among many idealistic young Filipinos who entered civic and advocacy spaces with a sincere desire to serve the people and contribute to social change,” the agency said.

Article continues after this 

The task force also said reports linked Dingding to individuals previously associated with NPA activities in Negros.

“No Filipino death should ever be celebrated as a victory—least of all the death of a young, educated and promising individual,” the NTF-Elcac added.

It added: “Behind every casualty is not just a name in a report, but a son, a friend, a classmate and a human life that once held immense possibility.”

Tug-ani, the official student publication of UP Cebu, said on Facebook that Dingding was a computer science alumnus and former student leader at the university.

He previously served in the UP Cebu University Student Council as vice chairperson in 2015, councilor in 2014 and second-year representative in 2013 and was also affiliated with the mass organizations Nagkahiusang Kusog sa Estudyante.

Within the university and the broader Cebu community, Dingding was known for advocating student rights, education and human rights.

Identities

The Army identified the four other fatalities as Jobert Casipong, also known as “John,” “Ruby” and “Ramram,” a member of the Southwest Front, Komiteng Rehiyon-Negros (KR-N) and a resident of Sipalay City, Negros Occidental; Gilbert Tingson, aliases “Ryan” and “Kolintong,” a member of Southwest Front-D, KR-N, also from Sipalay City; Rolando Dantes Jr., aliases “Mistah,” “Ana,” “Anyo,” “Arnel” and “Roman,” commanding officer of Southwest Front-D, KR-N and a resident of Sipalay City and Barangay Camalanda-an, Cauayan; and Alex Chavez Languita, alias “Axel,” a member of Southeast Front-D, KR-N, from Barangay Kabulakan, Santa Catalina, Negros Oriental.

The five were killed in a series of armed encounters with soldiers from the Army’s 15th Infantry Battalion in the hinterlands of Barangays Abaca and Poblacion in Cauayan.

Brig. Gen. Jason Jumawan, commander of the Army’s 302nd Infantry Brigade, said the group had been linked to the killings of 26 civilians in Negros Island since 2024, including three this year.

Jumawan said the victims were civilians accused by the rebels of being government informants. He added that Dantes had multiple warrants of arrest for murder.

Government troops recovered an M-14 rifle, an M60 machine gun, five M-16 rifles, an M203 grenade launcher, a grenade and four backpacks containing personal belongings from the encounter site, according to the Army.

Evacuation

Meanwhile, Cauayan Mayor John Rey Tabujara said 116 families, or 468 individuals, temporarily evacuated during the clashes on Saturday but were able to return home the following day.

Tabujara noted that the Cauayan municipal government declared the NPA persona non grata in 2024, a policy that remains in effect.

He condemned the “violence, intimidation and disturbance” allegedly caused by the NPA in the town.

“The local government of Cauayan will not tolerate any threat to civilian safety,” the mayor said in a statement posted on Facebook.

World.title: New Subic BOC chief vows to dispose of 118 overstaying containers
World.content:
UP FOR CLEARING Some of the overstaying refrigerated containers carrying confiscated perishable goods have been stranded for more than 300 days inside the Subic Bay International Terminal Complex. —JOANNA ROSE AGLIBOT

SUBIC BAY FREEPORT, ZAMBALES, Philippines — Newly appointed Bureau of Customs (BOC) Port of Subic District Collector Geniefelle Lagmay has vowed to expedite the clearing of 118 overstaying refrigerated containers that have become a major health and operational concern inside the freeport.

Lagmay, who officially assumed the post from outgoing District Collector Arnold Saulog on Monday, said he has already coordinated with the BOC central office—particularly the Legal Service and the Office of the Deputy Commissioner for Assessment and Operations Coordinating Group—to fast-track the disposition of the cargoes.

“Rest assured that we are trying our best and within weeks, we will have action on this,” Lagmay said in an interview.

Article continues after this 

READ: BOC: P47.4M smuggled agri-products blocked at Subic port

According to Lagmay, the delays may have stemmed from pending legal cases, failure of importers to lodge entries or pay duties or the shipments being completely abandoned.

The 118 refrigerated containers, carrying confiscated perishable goods, have been stranded at the Subic Bay International Terminal Complex (SBITC) for more than 300 days.

Appeal

SBITC management and nearby tourism stakeholders recently appealed to government authorities for immediate action, warning that the decomposing meat and food products have been emitting foul odors and consuming significant terminal power resources.

The issue now confronts Lagmay as he begins his tenure under strict directives from the national government.

Article continues after this 

READ: BOC dumps 5 containers of smuggled agricultural products

Last week, he was ordered to intensify efforts against the smuggling of agricultural products, cigarettes and vape products, while also strengthening revenue collection.

Article continues after this 

Despite acknowledging the seriousness of the backlog, Lagmay said the seized containers also reflect the bureau’s intensified antismuggling campaign.

“On one hand, it’s good that we have seized containers because it shows that the BOC is doing its job. We are intercepting illicit and unregulated cargoes,” he said.

He added: “But at the same time, it has become a concern because we have not been able to dispose of them immediately.”

Lagmay said he has instructed his team, in coordination with Saulog, to prioritize the processing and clearance of the overstaying shipments.

The new BOC Subic district collector acknowledged that removing the containers and transporting them to disposal facilities would likely spread foul odors along public roads.

Complaints

“We understand the impact this has on the surrounding communities, especially the local government unit, because the smell is already noticeable inside the pier. Nearby establishments are complaining and once these containers are transported on public roads, we expect there may be more complaints,” Lagmay said.

He appealed for the cooperation and understanding of local government units and residents, while also apologizing in advance for the inconvenience.

World.title: ‘Resign order’ vs BARMM education minister opposed
World.content:
COTABATO CITY, BARMM, Philippines — Thousands of supporters of the Moro Islamic Liberation Front (MILF) marched and staged a protest rally on Monday in front of the Bangsamoro government center to oppose Chief Minister Abdulraof Macacua’s letter asking Education Minister Mohagher Iqbal to resign.

The rally participants also called for the full implementation of the government-MILF Comprehensive Agreement on the Bangsamoro and the reinstatement of Al Haj Murad Ebrahim as Chief Minister of the Bangsamoro Autonomous Region in Muslim Mindanao (BARMM).

Protesters carried placards demanding Ebrahim’s reinstatement and expressing support for Iqbal to remain as minister of the Ministry of Basic, Higher and Technical Education (MBHTE).

Article continues after this 

READ: MILF vows cooperation with new peace adviser

The demonstrators filled the 300-meter, four-lane Gov. Gutierrez Avenue leading to the main entrance of the Bangsamoro Government Center beginning at 7 a.m.

The group also called for the reinstatement of 41 MILF-endorsed members of the Bangsamoro Transition Authority (BTA).

Police estimated the crowd at between 10,000 and 15,000 people.

READ: Iqbal tells Bangsamoro: We can’t support a candidate who’ll bring back past horrors

Article continues after this 

‘No due process’

Datswin Sangkula, spokesperson for the Recover BARMM Movement, said the protesters opposed Macacua’s letter directing Iqbal to step down despite the absence of due process and without any criminal or administrative charges filed against him.

In his letter to Iqbal, Macacua cited a report from the Commission on Audit (COA) on alleged discrepancies in MBHTE procurement bids amounting to more than P2.2 billion as basis for requesting the minister’s resignation.

Article continues after this 

Macacua said that “given the gravity of the findings and the enormity of the amount involved, the gains of good and moral governance enunciated by former Chief Minister Ahod Balawag Ebrahim and which we are currently pursuing, are in serious jeopardy.”

The acting chief minister noted that “the issue is not about Iqbal as a person, but about corruption. It just so happened that he is the minister.”

Macacua also described the MBHTE as “graft-ridden,” saying findings from the COA and the BTA Blue Ribbon Committee indicate that corruption exists within the ministry.

On Saturday, May 16, Iqbal rejected Macacua’s request for him to step down.

Preliminary findings

“I respectfully decline to resign at this time and I wish to place on record that I do not consent to any interpretation of my silence or any future action as constituting a constructive or deemed resignation,” Iqbal said.

World.title: MPD recommends raps vs 9 protesters over violence at Labor Day rally
World.content:
MAY DAY CLASH A tense standoff between Labor Day protesters and antiriot police leads to this scene on Manila’s Recto Avenue near Malacañang on Thursday. —NIÑO JESUS ORBETA

MANILA, Philippines — The Manila Police District (MPD) has recommended nine individuals to undergo preliminary investigations in connection with alleged violent incidents at a Labor Day rally there earlier this May.

Although it did not name the individuals in question, in a statement on Monday, the MPD said the protesters have been recommended to be investigated for tumults and other disturbances of public order; as well as violation of Batas Pambansa No. 880 or the Public Assembly Act.

“During the assembly, some protesters allegedly became unruly and attempted to breach barricades established by civil disturbance management contingents,” the MPD maintained.

Article continues after this

It further cited an instance in which some protesters set fire to effigies, prompting Bureau of Fire Protection personnel to attempt to extinguish the flames.

“However, some protesters reportedly obstructed their efforts and confronted them aggressively,” the MPD further said.

READ: Police, protesters trade barbs over violence at Labor Day rally

It also noted that a protester particularly supposedly punched a police officer in the face and stole the smartphone of another cop who was purportedly documenting the activity.

“The MPD respects and protects the constitutional right to peaceful assembly and the right to petition the government for redress of grievances. However, these activities must be conducted within the bounds of the law,” the police maintained.

Sectoral groups had mounted a protest in Manila last May 1 to call on President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. to address rising costs of basic goods.

Protesters aimed to continue their program at the United States Embassy to call for an end to its war against Iran, but the police blocked them along Kalaw Avenue, causing tensions between rallyists and law enforcers.

World.title: DPWH eyes dredging, flood interceptor projects in flood-prone Parañaque
World.content:
MANILA, Philippines — The government is eyeing a combination of dredging, drainage upgrades, detention basins and flood interceptor projects to address persistent flooding in Parañaque, Department of Public Works and Highways (DPWH) Secretary Vince Dizon said Monday.

During an inspection of flood-prone areas near Dr. Santos Avenue and Don Galo Creek with Parañaque Rep. Brian Yamsuan and local officials, the public works secretary noted that floodwaters in some communities, “minsan daw lampas tao ‘yung tubig dito.” (“would sometimes rise above a person’s height”)

According to Dizon, among the immediate interventions being considered are dredging operations in Villanueva Creek near Manila Memorial Park and in Don Galo Creek to restore water flow obstructed by garbage buildup and siltation.

Article continues after this 

READ: DPWH taps experts to ensure efficient plans for flood control projects

“You can see that the water is barely flowing anymore. That means the waterways are clogged, clogged with garbage and heavy siltation, and have already become too shallow,” Dizon said in an interview.

He explained that shallow waterways cause water to backflow into nearby roads and residential areas whenever water levels rise.

“Even if we declog the drainage system there, it would still be useless if the water level here is already higher and the water eventually flows back. The flooding will keep returning to the roads and homes,” he added.

The Department of Public Works and Highways is also studying the construction of detention basins beneath courts and open spaces, similar to projects implemented in Quezon City and Manila.

Article continues after this 

READ: DPWH drainage project in Parañaque ‘unnecessary, overpriced, delayed’

Dizon said some revetments or creek walls in the area also need to be elevated, with portions already programmed for implementation in 2027.

Article continues after this 

Despite funding limitations, Dizon said the government hopes to begin work this year on a proposed flood interceptor project along Dr. Santos Avenue that would run underneath Manila Memorial Park toward Villanueva Creek.

“Even with just P50 million, we should already begin the project this year so we can get started,” he said.

Yamsuan, meanwhile, said flooding problems in the city were worsened by long-neglected drainage and flood control projects.

“Sec. Vince saw that Parañaque has many catch basins, but he also saw the blockages and flooding caused by these long-neglected projects that have gone unattended for years,” Yamsuan said.

He also appealed for cooperation from private subdivisions and residents to allow the implementation of flood control projects in their areas.

“We really need your cooperation to allow us to do the projects inside your areas so we can implement projects that will help address the city’s overall flooding problem,” Yamsuan said.

World.title: Ridon says any further Senate leadership change won’t affect trial
World.content:
Bicol Saro party-list Rep. Terry Ridon —PHOTO FROM TERRY RIDON/FACEBOOK

MANILA, Philippines — Despite rumors of another leadership change in the Senate—just one week after Senate President Alan Peter Cayetano’s election—a member of the prosecution team believes any further shake-ups would not affect the impeachment trial against Vice President Sara Duterte.

In an online interview on Monday, Bicol Saro party-list Rep. Terry Ridon said he would not like to comment on something that has not happened yet. However, Ridon said that the only change that would happen, should a new Senate President be elected, is that he or she would have to take an oath as the presiding officer.

When the Senate convenes as an impeachment court, the Senate President takes an oath as the presiding officer. Cayetano did this earlier, taking his oath before Sen. Camille Villar when the Senate transitioned into an impeachment court.

Article continues after this 

READ: Senate convenes as impeachment court

“Well I don’t want to respond to the hypotheticals at this point, but just relating to the process itself, when there is a change in the leadership of the Senate, the only thing that would change is with regards to who the presiding officer is,” Ridon, a lawyer, said.

“The new presiding officer just needs to take an oath, if that will be the case at the future time,” he added.

Ridon said the Senate impeachment court “will still proceed as it should.”

Cayetano ascended to the Senate Presidency last May 11, as Senator Ronald “Bato” dela Rosa suddenly showed up at the plenary session after six months of absence.

Article continues after this 

READ: Cayetano retains Senate presidency as Zubiri, Ejercito join minority bloc

Dela Rosa’s presence proved to be significant as Cayetano won the seat through the minimum number of votes needed to unseat former Senate President Vicente Sotto III—13 votes.

Article continues after this 

However, just a week into his term as Senate President, there have been rumors that Cayetano is already on his way out. Some of the names rumored to replace Sotto are three former Senate Presidents themselves—Sotto, Senator Juan Miguel Zubiri, and Senator Francis Escudero.

READ: Escudero returning as SP? Sources say number reached to replace Cayetano

But when session resumed earlier, no changes to the Senate leadership was made.

Instead of change in the Senate President, Cayetano convened the Senate Impeachment Court, exactly a week after Duterte was impeached. A total of 257 House lawmakers voted in favor of adopting House Resolution (HR) No. 989, which contains Committee Report No. 261 and the articles of impeachment.

Prior to Duterte’s impeachment, three clarificatory hearings were held to discuss the grounds stated in the two remaining impeachment complaints. Last April 14, the panel discussed allegations of confidential fund (CF) misuse within the Office of the Vice President (OVP) and the Department of Education (DepEd), which she used to head before.

Some of the revelations made during the April 14 hearing were contained in the supplemental affidavit of Ramil Madriaga, Duterte’s former aide.

According to Madriaga, Duterte supposedly ordered her in December 2022 to deliver cash to allies as a way of “giving back.” Madriaga said four large duffel bags were unloaded from the vehicles, three of them were dark, and one was light-colored—containing around P30 million to P35 million each.

This is believed to be the P125 million confidential fund in 2022, which Madriaga said he liquidated in one day and not the reported 11 days.

READ: Madriaga: OVP’s 2022 secret funds spent in 1 day, not 11 days

On April 22, the panel tackled accusations that Duterte has unexplained wealth, and that she failed to disclose all her assets in her Statement of Assets, Liabilities, and Net Worth.

READ: AMLC confirms suspicious transactions made by Sara Duterte, kin
